dispositions.rationale: Repeats behavioural-outcome-1 of the merged record: BRF-A28 judges the skill text as the deliverable of S3.4, and the writer's behaviour is what F1 to F7 score under BRF-A16 to BRF-A20; neither claims the other.

Repeats obligation-reduction-1 of the merged record: the evaluation claims fidelity over its seven fixtures under the stochastic rule, and the per-brief guard is check (BRF-A8, BRF-A23), which BRF-A28 makes the skill require before every dispatch.
Repeats obligation-reduction-3 of the merged record: the writer sees one refusal shape whatever the code; F3 to F5 sample the refusal sources, and BRF-A28 reads the relay instruction in the skill.

F6 samples the writer's judgment on one infeasible check, and judging feasibility in code is out of scope by the spec's own list. The uniform four of five is the rule agents-config-9k9.479 records, and BRF-D8 states that five runs measure the scope sentence and never prove it.

Repeats behavioural-outcome-1 of the merged record: BRF-A28 judges the skill text as the deliverable of S3.4, and the writer's behaviour is what F1 to F7 score under BRF-A16 to BRF-A20; neither claims the other.
Repeats obligation-reduction-5 of the merged record: the installer stages the skill directory whole, and the evaluation runs the skill from source by full path (BRF-D8).
The installer prunes every test file and every evals/ directory by its own .installignore, and that staging check is the installer's gate, outside this spec's scope.
Repeats obligation-reduction-10 of the merged record: the helper is stdlib-only and its suite runs where no tracker storage exists; a second resolver is a code-review read.
Repeats obligation-reduction-12 of the merged record: the attestation is the record; the tree cannot observe the execution it attests (BRF-D8).
Repeats obligation-reduction-13 of the merged record: BRF-D8 states the repeat limit is an operator procedure because no output shows a retry.

Rests on the operator, as the merged record's obligation-reduction-14 states: nothing in the committed tree can observe a run that was never committed. The record now names the outputs that count and BRF-A35 refuses a sixth, but a replaced run that was never committed is invisible.

The fingerprint excludes evals/, where the scorer lives, so a scorer change alters no fingerprint and BRF-A33 keeps every lock current. Whether the operator dispatches writers anyway is an act the tree cannot observe.
Rests on the operator, as the merged record's obligation-reduction-14 states: nothing in the committed tree can observe a run that was never committed.

Reading a failed run and judging it a defect is the operator's act. BRF-D8 states the response, changing the skill, which voids the lock, as procedure, and the scope excludes judging in code what only a reading decides.

The sentence is agents-config-9k9.405.9's deliverable, and BRF-D6's 'leaves it alone' is a scope boundary, not a preservation obligation: that item's own criteria hold the sentence in place, and this spec's slices neither add nor remove it.

parts.statement: The passing F1 and F2 runs preserve criteria and evidence, and those fixtures meet the stated evaluation thresholds.
Other generated briefs, including assignments outside F1 and F2 and failed runs permitted by their locks, preserve exactly the assigned criteria and evidence.

obligations.source: Scope: 'A dispatch brief must carry exactly the criteria assigned to the work' and 'It must map each criterion to its planned check, apart from the criterion's text.'
obligations.statement: Generated briefs preserve exactly the assigned criteria and carry their evidence separately.

parts.statement: The passing F3 to F5 runs return the specified refusal reports, and those fixtures meet the evaluation thresholds.
The writer reports refusals rather than dispatching in other refusal cases and in runs not required to pass by those thresholds.

obligations.source: Scope: 'It must refuse when it cannot.' BRF-D4: 'The skill tells the writer to relay a refusal to its requester and dispatch nothing.'
obligations.statement: When criteria cannot be carried faithfully, the writer relays the refusal and dispatches nothing.

parts.statement: The passing F6 and F7 runs report their specified unready IDs instead of returning briefs, and those fixtures meet the evaluation thresholds.
The writer also reports and withholds other infeasible checks and unready briefs outside the passing runs represented by F6 and F7.

obligations.source: Scope: 'A criterion without a feasible planned check is reported unready.' BRF-D5: feasibility is the writer's judgment, and the skill tells the writer not to dispatch an unready criterion.
obligations.statement: The writer reports criteria without feasible planned checks as unready and does not dispatch them.

parts.statement: The skill's acceptance-criteria part and skeleton contain the required routing and reporting instructions.
The writer actually obtains the sections from emit and runs check before returning or dispatching a brief.

obligations.source: BRF-D1: 'The writer pastes both sections into the brief unchanged.' BRF-D6: 'Criteria and evidence come from emit, pasted unchanged, and check runs before dispatch.'
obligations.statement: The skill routes the writer through emit, unchanged pasting and check before dispatch.

parts.statement: brief_criteria.py is shipped beside SKILL.md.
Successful and unready emit outputs contain the full criteria and evidence sections, without a third section.

obligations.source: BRF-D1: 'The skill ships brief_criteria.py beside its SKILL.md' and 'Its emit mode prints exactly two Markdown sections.'
obligations.statement: The skill ships a helper beside SKILL.md that emits exactly the criteria and evidence sections.

parts.statement: Spec emission preserves all assigned entries and full text for small and large assignments.
Criteria-file emission preserves exactly the file's entries.

obligations.source: BRF-D2: '--spec PATH --ids ID,... reads the named entries' and '--criteria FILE reads a file holding only entries.' BRF-D3 defines fidelity as exact IDs and words. The what-if text states that neither mode bounds the criterion count.
obligations.statement: Spec and criteria-file sources produce their exact assigned criteria, including joined continuation text and large assignments.

parts.statement: Source readings use the stated entry grammar and preserve the resulting text.
The shared fixture covers each rule, both suites check expected readings, helper rule-breaking variants fail, and both parsers carry counterpart markings.

obligations.source: BRF-D2 lists the five grammar rules, requires counterpart markings, requires both suites to read one fixture, and requires each rule-breaking helper variant to fail a case.
obligations.statement: The helper follows the specified entry grammar, and its parser remains visibly paired with spec-lint through a shared, mutation-sensitive fixture.

parts.statement: Both suites' fixture tests fail when the shared fixture is absent.
The deployed skill excludes every test file and evals directory.

obligations.source: BRF-D2: 'Both suites fail when the fixture is absent. The installer prunes every test file along with evals/, so neither suite ever runs in a deployed tree, and nothing needs a skip.'
obligations.statement: Fixture absence fails repository tests, while test files and evals are excluded from deployment.

parts.statement: Empty assignments and empty criteria files refuse as no-criteria.
Absent assigned spec IDs refuse as unretrievable and name the IDs.
Missing or unreadable input files refuse as unreadable-source with the required path and assigned IDs.
Repeated assigned or defined IDs refuse as duplicate-id.
Nonblank criteria-file text outside entries refuses as malformed-criteria without an additional no-criteria fault.
Missing or multiple source flags refuse as source-conflict and name the supplied flags.
Refusals use empty stdout, one JSON fault object on stderr and exit 2.

obligations.source: BRF-D2 requires exactly one source flag. BRF-D4 specifies empty stdout, one fault object on stderr, exit 2, and the no-criteria, unretrievable, unreadable-source, source-conflict, duplicate-id and malformed-criteria cases.
obligations.statement: Invalid or unusable source inputs produce the specified refusal instead of pasteable output.

parts.statement: One refusal reports all detected faults, including both absent IDs in the specified case.

obligations.source: BRF-D4: 'One refusal names every fault the helper detects in the sources it can read. Two absent IDs therefore yield one refusal naming both.'
obligations.statement: A refusal aggregates every detected fault in readable sources.

parts.statement: Without checks, preserved criteria pass and every missing, added or altered ID fails with its ID named.
check shares emit's source refusals and refuses an unreadable brief.

obligations.source: BRF-D1 describes check against the source. BRF-D3 defines exact IDs, whitespace-normalized text and order independence. BRF-D4 includes unreadable briefs.
obligations.statement: check compares criterion IDs and normalized words, ignoring order and harmless whitespace changes, and refuses unusable inputs.

parts.statement: Complete planned checks emit exact evidence and exit 0; well-formed unassigned entries have no effect.
The criteria section is identical with absent, complete or incomplete checks.
check with checks accepts preserved criteria and evidence and rejects every missing, added or altered evidence ID.

obligations.source: BRF-D5 requires an evidence section containing exactly assigned IDs and their observation and pass rule. BRF-D3 defines evidence equality against emit from the same plan.
obligations.statement: Evidence maps exactly the assigned IDs to planned observations and pass rules, independently of the criterion text.

parts.statement: Every missing entry or blank field receives the specified reasons, and absent checks make every criterion unready.
Unready emission retains the full criteria section.

obligations.source: BRF-D5 defines the closed reason set, missing-key treatment, absent-checks treatment, stderr naming and exit 1.
obligations.statement: Missing or blank planned-check fields produce unready evidence, stderr identification and exit 1 without losing criteria.

parts.statement: Malformed checks refuse; absent fields are not malformed; unrelated keys have no observable effect.

obligations.source: BRF-D5 defines malformed JSON and object shapes, applies validation to assigned and unassigned entries, treats absent fields as blank, and ignores other keys.
obligations.statement: The checks file obeys the stated shape across all entries, while missing keys and unrelated keys receive the specified treatment.

parts.statement: Against the stub facade, emit uses the rendered criteria and makes no other facade call.
The helper never independently reads or resolves an item's acceptance field.
Missing render support and rendering failures refuse as render-failed with the item and cause.
A rendering with no criteria refuses as no-criteria.

obligations.source: BRF-D7: '--item runs work acceptance render ID' and 'It never resolves an item's acceptance field itself, since that would be a third resolver of LIFE-D1.'
obligations.statement: Item criteria come exclusively from work acceptance render, with specified rendering failures and empty-result behaviour.

parts.statement: python3 without third-party packages and uv run produce the same helper outputs and exit status.
Repeated unchanged helper and scorer runs are deterministic; emit and check write no files and independent concurrent runs share nothing.

obligations.source: BRF-D1 requires standard-library operation under uv run or python3. The what-if text states that emit and check never write, unchanged runs print the same result and concurrent runs share nothing. BRF-D8 describes mechanical scoring of stored outputs.
obligations.statement: The helper requires only the standard library and behaves consistently across runtimes, repeated runs and concurrent independent inputs.

parts.statement: The record contains an Opus resolved model ID, the fingerprint and the required fresh-context and native-Agent attestations.
The executions actually use that model, tool, source skill, task, context isolation and restricted dispatch arrangement.

obligations.source: BRF-D8 specifies Claude Opus through the native Agent tool, the source-tree skill by full path, fixed tasks, fresh contexts, returned output instead of dispatch, no subagent tool, a resolved model ID and operator attestations.
obligations.statement: The evaluation uses the specified writer execution protocol and records its identity, context and tool provenance.

parts.statement: The evaluation fixtures and stated seeded scorer cases receive their required form, preservation and evidence judgments.
A complete initial side below three passing runs fails without a retest.
A side at three of five awaits its retest, then passes only if all five retest runs pass.

obligations.source: BRF-D8 requires mechanical form scoring, separate F1 and F2 sides, four of five to pass, one retest at three of five, eight of ten after that retest, and failure below three.
obligations.statement: The scorer applies the fixture forms, separate sides and threshold rules.

parts.statement: Missing outputs, incomplete earned retests and missing scored files leave the fixture incomplete rather than locked or failed.
The operator performs no more than two repeats of a no-output run.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: 'A run with no output is repeated at most twice. It is then left pending and never scored as failed. The repeat limit is an operator procedure.'
obligations.statement: Missing outputs receive at most two repeats and then remain pending; incomplete attempts cannot lock.

parts.statement: Every performed run remains in the attempt and contributes under the fixed run-count and retest procedure.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: 'No run is discarded.'
obligations.statement: No performed evaluation run is discarded.

parts.statement: A mismatching computed fingerprint makes the lock noncurrent and excludes the fixture from the evaluation of record.
Matching locks remain current when other fixtures change, and unaffected fixtures are not rerun.

obligations.source: BRF-D8 defines the fingerprint and states: 'A lock is current while its fingerprint matches the tree. A change voids only the locks whose fingerprint it alters, and only those fixtures run again.'
obligations.statement: Lock currency follows each fixture's own fingerprint, and only affected fixtures lose their locks.

parts.statement: A scorer-only change uses stored outputs, dispatches no writer and retains still-passing locks.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: 'A change to the scorer dispatches no writer: the stored outputs are rescored, and a lock stands when its fixture still passes.'
obligations.statement: Scorer changes rescore stored outputs without dispatching writers and preserve locks whose fixtures still pass.

parts.statement: Committed evidence includes every attempt and all required files, with retests beside their original attempts.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: 'An attempt is committed under evals/runs/<run-id>/ with its outputs, its record and its report, whatever it shows, and a retest's five runs beside the attempt they extend. That rests on the operator.'
obligations.statement: Every attempt is committed with its outputs, record and report, including failed attempts and adjacent retests.

parts.statement: A demonstrated defect causes the required skill change, lock invalidation and fixture rerun.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: 'A failed run behind a lock is committed and read like any other, and a defect it shows is answered by changing the skill, which voids the lock and runs the fixture again.'
obligations.statement: A defect demonstrated by a failed run behind a lock is answered by changing the skill and reevaluating the affected fixture.

parts.statement: The LIFE-A32 sentence remains unchanged.
The rewritten skill passes the applicable content-lint gate, including its token caps.

obligations.source: BRF-D6: 'LIFE-A32's sentence on re-attack before use belongs to lifecycle S6 ... so this slice leaves it alone. Content-lint's token caps apply.'
obligations.statement: The skill rewrite preserves LIFE-A32's re-attack-before-use sentence and obeys content-lint's token caps.

parts.statement: The scorer scores the earlier attempt and refuses a later attempt with the same fingerprint.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: 'The scorer refuses a second attempt recording a fingerprint it has already scored, whether the fixture locked or failed.'
obligations.statement: A fingerprint gets one attempt and its earned retest; later attempts on that fingerprint are refused regardless of the earlier result.

parts.statement: Completion requires current generated-output locks for the preservation, evidence, refusal and readiness fixtures.

obligations.source: Scope identifies the generated brief as the consumer boundary. BRF-D9 states: 'The helper suites establish the mechanism. Only the evaluation of record establishes the parents at the generated brief.'
obligations.statement: Verification reaches the generated-brief boundary, and the evaluation of record supplies the parent evidence.

parts.statement: content-tests executes the helper and scorer suites, and ci executes the spec-lint fixture test; seeded suite failures make their gates fail.
S3.1 passes make content-tests and make ci.
S3.2 passes make content-tests.
S3.3 passes make content-tests.
S3.4 passes make content-lint.

obligations.source: The Continuations require make content-tests and make ci to exit 0 for S3.1, make content-tests to exit 0 for S3.2 and S3.3, and make content-lint to exit 0 for S3.4. The ordered slices assign the helper, scorer and spec-lint fixture tests to those deliverables.
obligations.statement: The advertised gates execute the relevant suites and pass for their implementation slices.

ground.reason: BRF-D6 promises that criteria and evidence come from emit and that check runs before dispatch. BRF-A28 verifies only that the skill contains instructions to do those things. Traceability names a content test for the writer's route. The generated-brief evaluation checks returned outputs, so it also cannot distinguish helper use from manually producing the same output.

objections.objection: The skill can pass its content check while writers skip the promised helper workflow.
objections.obligation: BRF-D6's requirement that writers obtain the sections from emit and run check before dispatch.

scenario.expect: The content test passes, and correctly constructed outputs can pass the generated-brief evaluation, while the writer never runs emit or check.
scenario.given: A skill containing all four instructions required by BRF-A28, with a writer that manually constructs criteria, evidence and reports matching the fixtures' expected outputs.
scenario.when: The BRF-A28 content test and BRF-D8 generated-brief evaluation run.

ground.reason: BRF-A16 and BRF-A17 observe fixed fixtures at a threshold that permits failed runs. They do not discharge the broader generated-brief fidelity promise.

objections.objection: A writer can pass the evaluation while changing or omitting assigned criteria in other briefs.

scenario.expect: The writer returns a brief that omits an assigned criterion, although every criterion check passes.
scenario.given: The helper satisfies its criteria and the writer passes F1 and F2, but mishandles assignments containing several hundred criteria.
scenario.when: The writer briefs a task with several hundred assigned criteria.

ground.reason: The generated-brief refusal checks represent zero criteria, an absent spec ID and an unreadable spec. They do not cover the other committed refusal cases.

objections.objection: The writer can dispatch after a refusal outside F3 to F5.

scenario.expect: The writer returns a brief instead of relaying the refusal and dispatching nothing.
scenario.given: All helper and evaluation checks pass, but the writer handles malformed checks files by inventing an evidence section.
scenario.when: The helper refuses a malformed checks file.

ground.reason: F6 represents one infeasible pass rule and F7 represents missing or blank fields. Their fixed runs do not discharge readiness handling for other infeasible checks or other generated briefs.

objections.objection: A writer can dispatch a criterion whose nonblank planned check is infeasible.

scenario.expect: The writer returns a brief without reporting the criterion as unready.
scenario.given: All checks pass, including F6, but a different criterion requires observing a private system to which the writer and subagent have no access.
scenario.when: The writer assesses that criterion's nonblank observation and pass rule.

ground.reason: BRF-A28 checks instructions in the skill. Output fidelity checks cannot establish that the writer executed emit or check.

objections.objection: The writer can produce accepted outputs while bypassing the required helper route.

scenario.expect: The returned brief passes the scorer even though the writer never ran emit or check.
scenario.given: The skill contains all four required instructions, and the writer manually reproduces the expected sections for every fixture.
scenario.when: The evaluation scores the returned briefs.

ground.reason: The criteria check helper behaviour and skill instructions, but none checks that brief_criteria.py ships beside SKILL.md.

objections.objection: The specified skill-local helper deliverable can be absent.

scenario.expect: Every criterion check passes while the skill directory lacks brief_criteria.py.
scenario.given: The helper is supplied elsewhere in the repository, the suites invoke that copy, and the skill directs the evaluation writer to it.
scenario.when: The skill directory is inspected as the deliverable promised by BRF-D1.

ground.reason: Repository fixture tests do not observe the deployed tree. No criterion checks the promised exclusion of the new test files.

objections.objection: A helper test file can be deployed alongside the skill.

scenario.expect: The deployed skill contains a test file, although the repository suites and gates pass.
scenario.given: The installer prunes evals directories but fails to recognize the new helper test file beside SKILL.md.
scenario.when: The installer stages the skill for deployment.

ground.reason: BRF-A13 observes rendered criteria and facade calls against a stub. It does not observe direct reads or independent resolution of an item's acceptance field.

objections.objection: The helper can introduce the third resolver BRF-D7 forbids.

scenario.expect: The helper independently resolves the item's acceptance field despite making only the permitted facade call.
scenario.given: The helper uses render when no local item storage exists, so the stub check passes, but also resolves local acceptance fields when storage is present.
scenario.when: emit --item runs in a real repository.

ground.reason: BRF-A26 observes record fields and attestations. It establishes their presence, not the execution conditions they assert.

objections.objection: An evaluation can lock using outputs produced outside the required writer protocol.

scenario.expect: The scorer accepts the record and locks the fixtures without the required native Agent executions in fresh contexts.
scenario.given: Conforming outputs were produced in reused contexts or by another model, but the record names Claude Opus and contains the required attestations.
scenario.when: The scorer evaluates the attempt.

ground.reason: BRF-A32 covers exactly three passing initial runs. BRF-A27's seeded two-failure cases do not cover a complete side below three passing runs.

objections.objection: A complete side below three passing runs can remain pending instead of failing.

scenario.expect: The scorer reports awaiting a retest instead of failed.
scenario.given: The scorer passes the defined seeded cases and actual evaluation locks, but a separate complete side has two passing and three failed initial runs.
scenario.when: The scorer processes that side.

ground.reason: BRF-A26 checks missing-output treatment, but no criterion observes the operator's repeat count.

objections.objection: A missing-output dispatch can be repeated beyond the committed limit.

scenario.expect: A fourth invocation produces an output that enters a passing attempt.
scenario.given: A dispatch and its two permitted repeats produce no output; the eventual record and all scored outputs satisfy the criteria.
scenario.when: The operator invokes the same dispatch again instead of leaving it pending.

ground.reason: The completeness check requires every scored output to exist. It does not require every performed run to be retained and scored.

objections.objection: Failed runs can be discarded within an attempt without triggering the second-attempt refusal.

scenario.expect: The scorer locks an attempt whose five retained outputs omit a failed run.
scenario.given: The operator replaces a failed initial run with an extra successful run and records only five successful outputs under one fingerprint.
scenario.when: The scorer checks the attempt's completeness and threshold.

ground.reason: BRF-A33 checks exclusion of a changed fingerprint. It does not check preservation of locks whose fingerprints remain unchanged.

objections.objection: A change to one fixture can invalidate unrelated current locks.

scenario.expect: The scorer drops an unrelated lock whose fingerprint still matches.
scenario.given: Every criterion check passes, but the scorer invalidates all locks whenever any fixture changes.
scenario.when: Only F1's fixture files change.

ground.reason: No criterion checks the scorer-change procedure or its prohibition on dispatching writers.

objections.objection: A scorer change can trigger new writer runs instead of rescoring stored outputs.

scenario.expect: Writers are dispatched again even though the stored outputs still pass the revised scorer.
scenario.given: All criterion checks pass and only the scorer has changed.
scenario.when: The evaluation is refreshed.

ground.reason: Directory completeness and current-lock checks do not establish that every attempt, including failed attempts, was committed with its record, report and outputs.

objections.objection: The evaluation can pass while its required committed evidence is incomplete.

scenario.expect: The passing evaluation exists in the working tree, while a failed attempt is absent from committed history.
scenario.given: Current locks and their files satisfy the scorer, but the operator leaves a failed attempt uncommitted.
scenario.when: The slice is declared complete.

ground.reason: The lock criteria permit a failed run behind a passing lock. No criterion checks the required response to a defect that run demonstrates.

objections.objection: A demonstrated skill defect can remain unresolved behind a current lock.

scenario.expect: The fixture remains locked without a skill change or a new evaluation.
scenario.given: Four runs pass and one fails; the failed run demonstrates a confirmed skill defect, and every criterion check passes.
scenario.when: The failed run is reviewed.

ground.reason: The content instruction check and lint gate do not compare the lifecycle sentence before and after the skill rewrite.

objections.objection: The rewrite can remove the sentence this slice promises to preserve.

scenario.expect: All criteria pass while LIFE-A32's re-attack-before-use sentence has been removed.
scenario.given: The rewritten skill contains the four instructions required by BRF-A28 and stays within token caps.
scenario.when: The acceptance-criteria part and skeleton are replaced.

ground.reason: BRF-A27 requires the scorer to fail a side that has exactly two failed runs of five, while BRF-D8 and BRF-A32 require that same side (three passes of five) to earn a retest and be reported as awaiting that retest, neither locked nor failed. The two verdicts cannot both hold for one side in one state.

objections.objection: The set lets an implementation pass BRF-A32 by reporting a three-of-five side as awaiting a retest while failing BRF-A27 on the seeded two-failed-runs set, or pass BRF-A27 by failing that side while violating BRF-D8's retest rule. A scorer cannot satisfy both on the same input.

scenario.expect: BRF-A27 demands the scorer fail the side and name its fixture; BRF-D8 and BRF-A32 demand the scorer report the side as awaiting a retest, explicitly neither locked nor failed — two incompatible verdicts for the identical state
scenario.given: An output set for a fixture in which a side has five scored runs, exactly two of them failing (the seeded set BRF-A27 describes), with no retest committed
scenario.when: the scorer scores the attempt and the result is judged against the criteria

ground.reason: For an attempt that has earned a retest whose five runs are not yet committed, BRF-A26 requires the scorer to report the fixture as incomplete (its 'a retest it earned has fewer than five more' clause, with missing outputs named as pending), while BRF-A32 requires the scorer to report the fixture as awaiting a retest. The set never states whether these are one report or two distinct verdicts, so the scorer's output vocabulary for this state is undecided.

objections.objection: The criteria permit two materially different scorer outputs for the same attempt state: an 'incomplete' report naming pending outputs (BRF-A26) or an 'awaiting a retest' report (BRF-A32). An implementer must choose the report shape without a criterion deciding it, and a test written against either reading can fail an implementation built to the other.

scenario.expect: Under BRF-A26 the report reads 'incomplete' with each missing output named as pending; under BRF-A32 it reads 'awaiting a retest' — different observable outputs, and the set names no decision that picks one
scenario.given: A committed attempt in which one side has exactly two failed runs of five and no retest runs committed
scenario.when: the scorer reports the fixture's state and that report is judged against the criteria

ground.reason: The set covers 'fewer than five scored outputs' (BRF-A26) and the earned retest's five more (BRF-A32), and BRF-D8 says 'no run is discarded', but no criterion or decision states what the scorer does with more runs than the five plus any earned retest — the document neither covers nor rules out the over-limit case, even though the operator repeat procedure (a no-output run repeated, whose original dispatch later returns) can produce it.

objections.objection: The criteria let through a scorer whose lock decision on an over-count attempt is undefined: a side with six committed outputs and four passing could be reported locked, failed, or incomplete depending on implementation, and the evaluation of record — the load-bearing verdict for the parent criteria — would differ across readings with no criterion to adjudicate.

scenario.expect: a defined verdict — the document implies every side is locked, awaiting retest, failed, or incomplete, but no criterion states which when the run count exceeds five plus an earned retest
scenario.given: an attempt for F1 holding six scored outputs (a no-output run was repeated, then the original dispatch returned and was committed, since no run is discarded), with four of the six passing on the preservation side
scenario.when: the scorer evaluates the attempt

ground.reason: BRF-A26 makes an attempt with a pending dispatch or missing attestation incomplete and unable to lock, and BRF-A34 refuses a second committed attempt recording the same fingerprint, but no criterion states whether an incomplete attempt burns the fingerprint — the document neither covers nor rules out re-attempting an unchanged fixture after an incomplete first attempt, so the 'what if it runs again' question has two contradictory readings.

objections.objection: The criteria let through a permanent lock-out: if an incomplete attempt counts as a committed attempt under BRF-A34, a transient operator failure (a dispatch that never returns after two repeats, or a missing attestation) leaves the fixture unable to lock and unable to re-attempt without an unrelated change to the skill, fixture, or model — with no criterion testing either resolution.

scenario.expect: either the second attempt is scored and the fixture can lock (incomplete attempts do not burn fingerprints) or it is refused (they do) — the document's refusal rule implies one reading, its completeness rule the other, and no criterion checks which
scenario.given: a committed attempt for F3 with four scored outputs and one dispatch pending, its record naming a fingerprint that still matches the tree
scenario.when: the operator commits a second attempt of five fresh runs recording the same fingerprint
